about: Radio and intercom for chapter 5: the powered descent to Taurus-Littrow. Time lines run to high gate and a little after (the autopilot is exact there); below that the Lunar Module Pilot's calls are cued by altitude (ft), by fuel and by events, so they stay right when you fly by hand. t = GET (seconds from liftoff). PDI 110:09:53, high gate 110:18:23, contact 110:21:58 on the autopilot. Original lines in the style of Apollo procedure; not quotes.

lines.text: Challenger, Houston. Standing by for ignition. Everything looks good.
Thirty seconds.
Ignition. Ten percent. Throttle up. We are on our way down.
Pressures look good. Windows up, and there is the Earth.
Challenger, Houston. You are go to continue powered descent.
Radar is locked on. Altitude and velocity lights are out.
Challenger, Houston. Accept the radar data. It looks good.
Throttle down. Right on time.
Challenger, Houston. You are go for landing.
Pitchover. There it is. The whole valley, right out the window.
The North Massif, and Camelot. We are right on target.
Four thousand feet, down forty.
Five hundred feet. Down twelve.
P sixty-six is yours whenever you want it.
Three hundred feet, down five.
Two hundred feet. Down four.
One hundred feet, down three. A little dust now.
Fifty feet, down two and a half. Lots of dust.
Thirty feet.
Ten feet.
Contact light!
Engine stop. Engine arm, off.
Houston, Challenger. We are on the ground, in the valley of Taurus-Littrow.
We copy you down, Challenger. You have a lot of happy people here.
Sixty seconds.
Thirty seconds.
You have it. P sixty-six.
Back to the computer.
Too hard. Let's run that again from high gate.
